title: kb_job reads a submitted job's state and log without blocking and kb_job_cancel stops it, so a session follows a land, done or stage-back with the tools it already has
goal: The kb MCP server lists kb_job (job or item or state to list; lines for the log tail; readOnlyHint true) and kb_job_cancel (job; readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint true, idempotentHint true) with KB_BACKLOG_WRITE_TOOLS=1; kb_job returns ops_service.status(job) (or ops_service.list(item, state)) as structuredContent with state, exit, step, started, ended and, when the job has ended, its result envelope, plus the log's last lines from ops_service.tail(job, lines), and a follow hint naming coord_wait with kind progress and the job's item; it never blocks on the job (this server answers one request at a time: coord_wait holds it for at most 60 s, so a long wait is the Bash route, coord.py wait --kind progress --item ID in a background shell); an unknown job is a tool error; kb_job_cancel calls ops_service.cancel(job) and returns the new state

run: import sys,os,tempfile,importlib;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");os.environ["KB_BACKLOG_WRITE_TOOLS"]="1";d=tempfile.mkdtemp();open(d+"/ops_service.py","w").write("S={\"J-test0001\":{\"job\":\"J-test0001\",\"verb\":\"land\",\"item\":\"ST-abcdefgh\",\"state\":\"running\",\"exit\":None,\"step\":\"rebase\"}};status=lambda j:S[j];list=lambda item=None,state=None:[v for v in S.values()];tail=lambda j,lines=20:[\"step rebase\"];cancel=lambda j:dict(S[j],state=\"cancelled\")");sys.path.insert(0,d);importlib.invalidate_caches();import kb_mcp;call=lambda n,**k:kb_mcp.handle({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":n,"arguments":k}})["result"];tools={t["name"]:t for t in kb_mcp.tool_list()};assert tools["kb_job"]["annotations"]["readOnlyHint"] is True and tools["kb_job_cancel"]["annotations"]["readOnlyHint"] is False,"annotations";r=call("kb_job",job="J-test0001",lines=5);s=r.get("structuredContent") or {};assert not r["isError"] and s.get("state")=="running" and s.get("step")=="rebase","kb_job",r;assert "coord_wait" in str(s.get("follow")),s;assert call("kb_job",job="J-nope0000")["isError"],"unknown job";c=call("kb_job_cancel",job="J-test0001");assert (c.get("structuredContent") or {}).get("state")=="cancelled",c

notes: Evidence 2026-11-08. coord_wait tool caps a hold at 60 s because this server answers one request at a time (kb_mcp.py:1003), so kb_job reads state and returns at once; a long follow is coord.py wait --kind progress --item ID (a Bash run_in_background shell or the Monitor tool, whose task notification wakes an idle session; docs: Bash run_in_background and background tasks, code.claude.com tools-reference, read 2026-11-08). Claude Code per-server timeout is wall-clock and progress notifications do not extend it; stdio idle window 30 minutes (docs mcp#time-limits-on-mcp-tool-calls, 2026-11-08). MCP spec options for later (kb/public/mcp/tasks-extension.md:12-26, DOC S718): a server may answer tools/call with CreateTaskResult (resultType task, taskId, ttlMs, pollIntervalMs) when the client declares io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks, polled with tasks/get, cancelled with tasks/cancel; progress notifications need a progressToken from the client (progress.mdx). Claude Code supports MCP tasks in public beta from v2.1.304, terminal CLI sessions, Agent SDK and stream-json sessions only, not subagents, not VS Code or desktop (docs read 2026-11-08). The job record this story reads is the durable handle the spec's task needs, and a stdio server's tasks survive its exit only when the work lives outside it, which the service gives: a tasks adapter (the server advertising the extension in server/discover and mapping tasks/get and tasks/cancel to status and cancel) is a later story, not filed here, because it helps interactive sessions only. Pairing: reads ops_service.status, tail, list, cancel from plan/ops-service's half.
